cases.description: The initial active scene and its first scene-delivery callback are observed on the main thread.
Frame, fixed, and late callbacks are each delivered without cross-subscriber failure propagation.
Named keyboard, mouse, and gamepad actions report pressed, held, released, axes, conflicts, rebinding, and UI-focus suppression.
Player/camera aim, health damage/heal, and nested control leases operate and restore controls.
Ray/shape queries, entity transforms and motion, held-item operations, and native interaction prompts/callbacks operate through safe handles.
A package bundle and prefab load asynchronously, spawn through an opaque handle, and are destroyed without leaks.
Non-positional and positional framework audio cues play and release through lifetime-owned handles.
Validated config migration, installation-local typed storage, localization, commands, and diagnostics survive a reload.
HUD, window, modal, toast, high contrast, UI scale, reduced motion, focus, and teardown use TopiaForgeUi.
Scene/world/gamemode registration, loading, pause actions, session lifecycle, and save-aware teardown complete cleanly.
Robot spawn/body/health/movement, targets, objectives, dialogue, brain query, voice input, and custom interaction run without consumer native APIs.

The declared multiplayer module resolves through the extension boundary, binds generated state/command/event codecs, and executes them canonically through a ready interactive client-plus-server standalone loopback session.

Declared required providers and the installed optional UGC provider resolve exactly once; an absent optional dependency does not block the consumer; singleton conflicts, multiple-provider ordering, deterministic selection, and early release are enforced.
Unavailable or drifted game bindings return stable results and reasons without crashing the mod or startup.

Automatable core and noninteractive module resource families complete ten in-session acquisition/release/reacquisition cycles with callback-stop and inactive-handle assertions. Hardware-, dialogue-, robot-, pause-, and session-specific handles are exercised by their dedicated live cases; offline lifecycle tests cover load/unload/reload and partial-load failure.
